chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from al-Nu'man ibn 'Abd al-Salam, from Abi Hanifah, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who said to another, “O wicked one,” and he said: “There is no hadd punishment upon him, but he is to be subjected to ta'zir.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man; the person committing the statement in question
key_terms.لَا حَدَّ: no fixed prescribed legal punishment applies
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: he is given ta'zir, a discretionary disciplinary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone says to another person, 'O fasiq'?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who insults another by calling him a fasiq. The ruling states that the fixed hadd punishment does not apply in this case, but discretionary chastisement (ta'zir) is imposed instead.
